name: Multiple Unlocks of a Critical Resource
principle: Code unlocks or releases a critical resource more times than it locks or acquires it. The extra unlock can expose protected state, corrupt lock accounting, increase semaphore permits, or cause crashes and unexpected state.
detection_signals: same pthread_mutex_unlock(&m) reachable twice after one pthread_mutex_lock(&m)
same std::mutex::unlock() or std::unique_lock::unlock() reachable twice after one lock()
same LeaveCriticalSection(&cs) or ReleaseMutex(h) reachable twice after one EnterCriticalSection/WaitForSingleObject
same sem_post(&s) reachable more times than sem_wait(&s) on an error path
Java Lock.unlock() called in both catch and finally for one lock.lock()
Java Semaphore.release() called on a path where acquire() did not succeed
duplicate unlock in cleanup labels, goto fail paths, or early-return branches for the same lock variable
negative_signals: C++ std::lock_guard or std::scoped_lock owns the mutex and no manual unlock() is called
C++ std::unique_lock checked with owns_lock() before unlock() and ownership is cleared after unlock
Java lock.lock(); try { ... } finally { lock.unlock(); } with no other unlock for that lock
boolean acquired flag set only after successful lock/acquire and tested before unlock/release
all control-flow paths have one unlock/release for each successful lock/acquire on the same resource
false_defense_traps: Calling unlock in both an error branch and a common cleanup/finally block
Using a cleanup label without nulling or clearing the ownership flag after unlock
Calling Semaphore.release() to compensate for a failed or timed-out acquire()
Assuming recursive/reentrant locks make extra unlocks safe
Catching and ignoring IllegalMonitorStateException or mutex unlock errors
verification_focus: For each lock/acquire that can succeed, can any control path perform more than one unlock/release on the same resource ownership?

consequence_chains.trigger: extra unlock releases mutual exclusion while protected state is still being accessed
consequence_chains.consequence: data race, memory corruption, or integrity loss

consequence_chains.trigger: extra sem_post/Semaphore.release increases available permits beyond intended capacity
consequence_chains.consequence: resource exhaustion, crash, or denial of service

patch_principle: Make lock and unlock counts match on every control-flow path.
Use RAII, try-with-resources, or try/finally to centralize release ownership.
Track ownership with an acquired flag when acquisition can fail or time out.
After manual unlock/release, clear the ownership state to prevent later cleanup from unlocking again.
